After opening a file from storage, check Tune-Frequency, Sample Rate and File Format: if they are wrong, the file doesn't play correctly. RF Analyzer fills them in from the file name where it can (see File Source), but that doesn't always succeed.

docs.title: Start the Analyzer
docs.text: The Quickstart section briefly explains all necessary steps to receive signals with the app. Detailed information about all UI elements can be found in the section User Interface and the following sections (SDR Source, FFT & Waterfall Display, Demodulation, Recording and Settings).

docs.title: SDR Device Not Recognized
docs.text:
If you get errors like "Source not available" or "Error with Source", the app is not able to communicate with the SDR device.

Possible reasons are:

  • Wrong SDR selected in Source Tab.
  • Phone’s USB port doesn’t provide enough power.
  • USB OTG adapter is faulty.
  • Another app is already using the SDR.

Solution:

  1. Try a powered USB hub.
  2. Ensure no other apps are using the SDR.
  3. Try different USB OTG adapters.
  4. Turn on logging in the Settings and look in the log file for more details.

USB permission denied

Android asks once for permission to use the SDR. If you denied it, tap Start again and allow access.

docs.title: Network Sources (rtl_tcp, KiwiSDR)
docs.text:
• Android 17 and newer: a server in your own network (rtl_tcp, a local KiwiSDR) needs RF Analyzer's local network permission. If Android no longer asks, allow it in the app's settings under Permissions → Nearby devices.
  • Short network stalls (up to 15 seconds) are bridged; after that the source stops with "Streaming stopped unexpectedly".
  • A KiwiSDR with no free channel slots is busy: pick another receiver.

docs.title: Purchase Not Recognized
docs.text: Purchases belong to the Google account that is active in the Play Store. Switch the Play Store to the account you bought with, return to RF Analyzer and tap Check again in the About tab.

docs.title: SDR Stops During Use (USB Connection Lost)
docs.text:
A loose USB plug or cable makes the SDR disconnect for a moment; the app then shows "... stopped streaming unexpectedly (USB connection lost?)". When the same SDR is connected again within 10 seconds, the analyzer restarts by itself - also with the app in the background, which stays there. Meanwhile the notification says "Waiting for ... to be reconnected"; its Stop button ends the wait.

When the SDR comes back, Android asks whether to open RF Analyzer for it; tick Always open RF Analyzer when ... is connected so that later reconnects work without the question. (Outside of these 10 seconds, and unless Start When an SDR Is Plugged In is enabled, Android doesn't offer RF Analyzer when an SDR is plugged in.)

docs.title: Performance Issues (Slow FFT, Choppy Audio)
docs.text:
Older hardware might not be powerful enough to ensure smooth operation of the app. In this case try the following:

  • Reduce the sample rate of the source.
  • Lower the Max Frame Rate in the Display tab.
  • Keep the Waterfall Speed at 30 fps or below: above that, the FFT frames overlap and cost more processing.
  • With Manual FFT Size on, choose a smaller FFT Size (otherwise it is chosen automatically).

If the app shows an Overload warning, see Processing Overload.

docs.title: Processing Overload
docs.text:
The app processes the signal of the SDR in real time: every second of signal has to be filtered, demodulated and decoded within one second. If your device is too slow for the current settings, it can't keep up and has to throw parts of the signal away. When this happens, the Demodulation tab shows the warning chip Overload – samples dropped; tap its ? to open this page. The audio stutters or is choppy. The chip disappears a few seconds after the overload stops.

What you can do (start at the top, it usually helps most):

  1. Reduce the sample rate of the source in the Source tab. This lowers the load of the whole processing chain. You see less bandwidth in the FFT, but the demodulator only needs the part around the channel anyway.
  2. Lower the Max Frame Rate and the Waterfall Speed in the Display tab; with Manual FFT Size on, also the FFT Size. Drawing the waterfall competes with the demodulator for processing power.
  3. Enable Low Performance Mode and lower the filter quality until the warning goes away.
  4. Close other apps running in the background and turn off battery saver mode, which slows down the processor.

Details for the curious: enable Show Debug Information to see the load of the busiest processing stage in the top right corner of the FFT (green below 70%, yellow up to 100%, red above), and, during an overload, how much of the signal was dropped and where.

docs.title: Poor Signal Quality / High Noise
docs.text:
• Use a good antenna & place it in an open area.
  • Disable automatic gain and manually adjust gain.
  • Increase sample rate to reduce aliasing (HackRF).

docs.title: App Crashes
docs.text:
• If possible, submit crash reports via Android.
  • RF Analyzer can log system errors; check the Settings.

docs.title: User Interface
docs.text:
The app is designed to give you interactive insights into radio signals, whether you are analyzing live signals from an SDR or replaying recorded IQ data. The user interface is structured to provide both real-time spectrum visualization and intuitive controls to configure your setup.

The UI consists of two main components:

  • FFT and Waterfall Plot - Displays the real-time frequency spectrum and signal history over time.
  • Control Drawer - Allows you to configure the analyzer, select input sources, and manage settings.

docs.title: FFT and Waterfall Plot
docs.text: When the analyzer is running, the FFT plot provides a live view of the frequency spectrum, while the waterfall plot gives a history of past signals, scrolling downwards as new data arrives.

docs.title: Interacting with the FFT Plot
docs.text:
You can explore the frequency spectrum in several ways:

  • Scrolling Left/Right - Move the center frequency up or down.
  • Pinch-to-Zoom - Adjust the frequency resolution for a more detailed or broader view.
  • Quick Tune & Zoom - Long-press an empty spot in the FFT or waterfall until a small control appears, then drag without lifting your finger: up/down zooms, left/right fine-tunes the channel. The first direction you drag in stays until you lift the finger; with demodulation off, only zooming works. A second finger switches to pinch-to-zoom.
  • Power Level Axis - Located on the left, this shows signal strength in dBFS. It can be scrolled up/down or zoomed using pinch gestures.
  • Autoscale Button - Found in the Display tab (FFT & Waterfall), this automatically adjusts the vertical dB scale for the best signal visibility. The Display tab also has a button to reset the scale and a slider to fine tune the vertical viewport.

The FFT plot is the heart of the RF Analyzer, and these interactive tools help you navigate and fine-tune your view of the spectrum.

docs.title: Control Drawer
docs.text: The control drawer is your main hub for adjusting settings. It appears at the bottom of the screen (or as a side panel in landscape mode). Drag the handle at its edge to open or close it. The tabs are shown as icons; the selected tab also shows its name.

docs.title: Available Tabs
docs.text:
• Source - Select and configure your signal input.
  • Demodulation - Set up signal demodulation (AM, FM, etc.).
  • Recording - Record raw IQ samples or the demodulated baseband to a file and manage recordings.
  • Display - Adjust FFT and waterfall display settings like scaling and resolution.
  • Settings - General application preferences.
  • About - App version, the manual, the tutorials (Quick Start, Bookmark Manager, What's New), your license and the purchase options, acknowledgments and licenses.

A Bookmark Manager screen can be accessed via the button floating above the control drawer or from the demodulation tab.

Let’s start with the Source Tab, which is the first step in setting up your analyzer.

docs.text:
Data on your device. Settings, bookmarks, station lists, recordings and the packets decoded in the Digital tab are stored on your device only. Uninstalling the app, or clearing its storage in Android's settings, deletes all of it. Recordings and exports leave the device only where you share or save them.

Backups. If backups are turned on, Android includes RF Analyzer's settings and bookmarks in your device backup in your Google account. Your location, the KiwiSDR password, your recordings, the decoded packets and the app's log file are left out of it. When you move to a new phone directly from the old one (by cable or Wi-Fi), Android copies all of the app's data to the new phone.

Location. RF Analyzer estimates your country on the device (mobile network, SIM, time zone, language) to choose band plans and station lists. Optionally you can choose your country, enter a grid locator or allow access to the device location (approximate, to about 2 km), for the maps, distances and nearby stations. Your location stays on your device: it is not sent anywhere and not included in backups.

Internet connections. RF Analyzer connects only to the servers below. Each of them sees your IP address and what is requested, under its own privacy policy:

  • SDR servers you connect to: rtl_tcp servers and KiwiSDR receivers (a KiwiSDR's operator can see the frequency you listen to), and the public KiwiSDR list (kiwisdr.com)
  • map tiles from OpenFreeMap (openfreemap.org) for the area you view
  • station lists: the digital station list (demantz.github.io, GitHub Pages; updated automatically) and, if you enable them, EiBi (afu-base.de), POTA (pota.app) and SOTA (sota.org.uk)
  • Google's time servers (time.android.com, time.google.com) for FT8's clock correction
  • Google Play, for purchases (Google Play version)

The user manual is part of the app and loads nothing from the internet. Links you tap (for example QRZ.com, aprs.fi or FlightAware) open in your browser.

Purchases (Google Play version). Purchases are processed by Google Play under Google's privacy policy; the developer receives only the order information Google Play provides, no payment details.

It processes the radio samples RF Analyzer passes to it in memory only and returns the decoded results to RF Analyzer, which stores and shows them as described above. The only thing the extension stores itself is whether you have seen its tutorial.
